sovereign_country.strategic_role: 极速离岸证券与外汇交易商持牌（VFSC）、轻资产免税出海

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Overseas Direct-Operated Hotpot Dining and Condiment Supply

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Vanuatu International Company regime, Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English common law, French civil law and customary law applied at unitary national level)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Vanuatu is a WTO Member (acceded 24 April 2012).
PACER-Plus (Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus) regional trade and economic integration framework.

No dedicated bilateral investment treaty or double taxation agreement specifically covering restaurant-sector outward investment has been identified; protection is derived from the International Companies Act and general contract law.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act [CAP 222] (as amended), Companies Act [CAP 191], Anti-Money Laundering and Proliferation Financing Act No. 13 of 2017, Anti-Money Laundering and Proliferation Financing Regulations 2017, and VFSC Beneficial Ownership Directive requiring each International Company to identify and record natural persons ultimately owning or controlling 25% or more.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (confidential UBO file maintained by the VFSC and accessible to Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit, law enforcement and competent authorities; not available in open public registry search)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of valid passport for each director, shareholder and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of the country of citizenship or a licensed notary public in that country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification followed by consular legalization at the nearest Vanuatu diplomatic mission or through the Vanuatu Ministry of Foreign Affairs; apostille is not accepted because Vanuatu is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds certificate for each funding beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank or financial institution maintaining the remitter account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank official signature notarized and consular legalized for use in Vanuatu; original or certified copy must be presented to the VFSC-licensed registered agent.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation, certificate of good standing and register of directors for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country company registry or equivalent competent authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Home-country notarization and consular legalization by Vanuatu consular office; apostille path is inapplicable for use in Vanuatu.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential/business address for each UBO and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, bank, municipality or recognized government administrative body
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized true copy and consular legalization; documents older than 90 days are rejected.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association or equivalent constitutional document of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or registered agent of the shareholder in its home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy notarized and consular legalized; a certified English or French translation must accompany the document.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UK sanctions list and the Vanuatu domestic list maintained under the Counter-Terrorism and Transnational Organised Crime Act No. 5 of 2005. Politically Exposed Persons must be identified under the Anti-Money Laundering and Proliferation Financing Act No. 13 of 2017, subjected to enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification and senior management approval before incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) Company Registry - International Companies online filing system, accessible through VFSC-licensed registered agents (www.vfsc.vu).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory company name must be registered in Latin script using English or French; if the intended hotpot restaurant brand is in Chinese or any non-Latin script, a VFSC-approved English/French transliteration must be the registered statutory name. The Chinese script may appear only as a secondary trade name on overseas restaurant signage and marketing materials, not as the exclusive registered company name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: An extension request must be filed with the VFSC through the licensed registered agent no later than three working days before expiry; the VFSC may grant a discretionary extension of up to 30 days upon payment of the prescribed extension fee. If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant must file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar of International Companies within 14 days of the rejection notice, stating the grounds of objection, evidence of non-conflict with existing names, and a proposed alternative name. If the Registrar upholds the rejection, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Vanuatu Supreme Court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office address is not permissible as the statutory registered office of an International Company. The company must maintain a physical registered office in Vanuatu supplied by a VFSC-licensed registered agent, normally located in Port Vila or Luganville. A virtual office may be used only for overseas restaurant back-office and mail handling outside Vanuatu.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate: approximately 5% to 10% annual probability that the VFSC or the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit conducts an unannounced inspection of the registered agent's records for AML/CFT compliance; the probability of physical inspection of the overseas hotpot restaurant premises is below 1% absent a complaint, sanctions alert or PEP-related red flag.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: VFSC statutory name search, name reservation and priority clearance including one alternative name
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Gazetted statutory fee under the International Companies (Fees) Regulations.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and consular legalization of identity, address, bank reference and corporate documents for four UBO/director principals
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public, home-country competent ministry and Vanuatu consular mission
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market tariff for notarial and consular authentication; no fixed Vanuatu statutory tariff.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT customer due diligence and UBO identification/piercing file preparation by VFSC-licensed registered agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for licensed agents' KYC and UBO compliance files.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of International Company constitutional documents, shareholder resolutions, registered office acceptance and corporate powers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Professional fee based on agreed engagement scope and prevailing Vanuatu legal market rates.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: VFSC incorporation registration fee and issuance of Certificate of Incorporation for the International Company
Licensed registered agent and physical registered office in Vanuatu for the first annual period
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Annual agent service fee at prevailing market benchmark.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certificate of good standing and incumbency for any corporate shareholder from its home jurisdiction registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Government or registry tariff applicable in the shareholder's country of incorporation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified English/French transliteration and translation of the Chinese hotpot brand name into the statutory International Company name
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate for certified translation and transliteration conformity review.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Secure international courier and document return between foreign principals, notary, consulate and VFSC registered agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Quoted courier fee at prevailing international express rates.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act No. 32 of 1992 (Cap. 222) of Vanuatu, particularly sections 5 (Incorporation), 6 (Memorandum of Association), 7 (Name restrictions), 39 (Registered Office), 40-52 (Directors and officers); read together with the Foreign Investment Act 2019 and the Business Licence Act [Cap. 248] for onshore restaurant operations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), Companies Registration Department, Port Vila, Republic of Vanuatu
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation issued under section 5 of the International Companies Act 1992, upon lodgment of the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association (Form AIC-1) with the VFSC Companies Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for an International Company; authorised capital may be denominated in any currency and may be as low as one share, with no escrow deposit, capital duty, or capital contribution certificate required at incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: IT IS RESOLVED THAT: (1) the incorporation of the Company as an international company under the International Companies Act, Cap. 222 be ratified; (2) the subscriptions to the authorised share capital be accepted and share certificates issued to the initial members; (3) the registered office be established at the licensed registered agent's address in Port Vila, Vanuatu, and the registered agent be appointed; (4) the persons named in the consent forms be appointed as directors; and (5) the directors be authorised to open bank accounts, execute lease agreements, and file all business, food-safety, environmental and fire-safety licence applications required for the hotpot restaurant operation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), Companies Registration Department (filed through a VFSC-licensed registered agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a company-name search in the VFSC register and reserve the proposed International Company name. The name must end with 'Limited' or its approved abbreviation, must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company in Vanuatu, and must not contain restricted words (e.g., 'bank', 'trust', 'insurance') without a separate licence. Submit two ranked name alternatives to preserve priority.
required_dossiers: Certified passport copy or certificate of authentication for each beneficial owner and proposed director
Name reservation instruction letter setting out two alternative corporate names
Signed declaration confirming the proposed name is not misleading and is available for use
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity, misleading content, or restricted wording, the registered agent may file a revised alternative name within 14 days of the refusal notice without loss of priority, or submit a written administrative review request to the VFSC Regulation Division for reconsideration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution and Notarisation of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC-licensed registered agent in conjunction with a Vanuatu notary public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Memorandum and Articles of Association in conformity with the schedule forms of the International Companies Act, Cap. 222, including the authorised share capital statement, object clause, and limitation of liability of members. The subscriber must execute the memorandum before a notary public in Vanuatu or in a recognised foreign notarial jurisdiction, and each initial director must execute a consent to act.
required_dossiers: Memorandum of Association (executed and notarised)
Articles of Association (executed)
Consent to Act as Director forms for each initial director
Subscriber statement recording share allocation and class of shares
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Documents returned by the VFSC or the notary for correction will be revised and re-executed by the subscriber; any non-conforming articles are redrafted to comply with mandatory provisions of the International Companies Act, and the notarisation is repeated without the need for court intervention.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Registered Agent and Adoption of Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC registration department with a VFSC-licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a registered agent licensed under the International Companies Act 1992, execute the registered-office services agreement for a physical address in Port Vila, and obtain the agent's written consent to act as registered agent and registered office. The agent will maintain the company's statutory registers and receive service of process on behalf of the company.
required_dossiers: Registered Agent Appointment and Consent Form
Registered Office Address Certificate issued by the agent
Signed service-of-process and compliance agreement between the company and the agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed agent's licence has lapsed or its address facility is rejected, the company will promptly appoint a substitute VFSC-licensed agent and file a fresh consent, curing the deficiency before the VFSC-imposed deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application with the VFSC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), Companies Registration Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge Form AIC-1 (Application for Incorporation) together with the signed Memorandum and Articles of Association, registered agent consent, director and subscriber particulars, and evidence of payment of the prescribed government filing fee. The VFSC examines the application for statutory formalities under section 5 of the International Companies Act 1992 and registers the company as an International Company with no income tax liability on foreign-source income.
required_dossiers: Form AIC-1 (Application for Incorporation of an International Company)
Memorandum and Articles of Association (signed and notarised)
Registered Agent Consent and Registered Office Certificate
Consents to Act as Director and subscriber identity documentation
Proof of payment of the VFSC incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VFSC issues a requisition or suspension notice, the agent will cure the stated defects within 14 days and resubmit; if the application is rejected, a fresh application with corrected dossiers and a new fee payment is filed, and for VFSC-error rejections an administrative review and fee credit may be requested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Tax-Exempt Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission as registrar and statutory authority under the International Companies Act and the Income Tax Act [Cap. 181]
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the VFSC issues the Certificate of Incorporation in the chosen company name. The International Company is thereafter exempt from Vanuatu tax on all foreign-source revenue, and the certificate together with the VFSC tax-status confirmation letter are used for bank account opening and licensing procedures before the municipal and industrial authorities.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by the VFSC
Register of Directors and Register of Members opened by the registered agent
VFSC tax-exemption confirmation letter (where issued) for banking and licensing purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains clerical errors in the company name, date, or capital particulars, the registered agent files a VFSC administrative correction request for re-issuance; no re-initiation of the incorporation procedure is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution, Share Subscription and Opening of Statutory Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and corporate secretary of the International Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the inaugural board meeting and pass the first board resolution ratifying the incorporation, accepting the share subscriptions set out in the subscriber statement, adopting the registered office, appointing the directors and officers, and authorising the issuance of share certificates. Open the statutory register of members, register of directors, register of charges, minute book, and if adopted, the company seal. Approve the bank mandate and instruct counsel to file the restaurant trade licence, foreign investment certificate, food-safety and environmental applications.
required_dossiers: Minutes or written resolutions of the first board meeting
Share subscription schedule and executed share certificates
Statutory registers of members, directors and charges
Bank authorised-signatory resolution and mandate form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any irregularity in the minutes or share allocation is cured by a supplemental board resolution; a defective director appointment is ratified by the board; and any inconsistency with the Memorandum and Articles is corrected by resolution of the board or, where required, by shareholder resolution.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Tourism, Trade, Commerce and Ni-Vanuatu Business; Vanuatu Investment Promotion Authority (VIPA); Port Vila Municipal Council Business Licence Office; Department of Customs and Inland Revenue under the Business Licence Act [Cap. 248]
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Licence (Restaurant and Tourism Trade) under the Business Licence Act [Cap. 248], together with a Foreign Investment Certificate (FIC) under the Foreign Investment Act 2019 for the overseas-direct-operated hotpot dining and condiment supply business

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environmental Protection and Conservation (DEPC), Ministry of Climate Change, Vanuatu
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 - Preliminary Environmental Assessment (PEA) registration tier; a full Environmental Impact Assessment report is not mandated for a single-site urban hotpot restaurant connected to municipal water and sewerage, subject to DEPC screening under the Environmental Protection and Conservation Act No. 12 of 2003 (as amended).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater must be discharged into the municipal sewerage network or a DEPC-approved grease-trap and septic system with no raw effluent to surface water; cooking oil and grease must be intercepted and disposed of by a licensed waste contractor; kitchen exhaust, flue and ventilation emissions (PM10, odour and volatile organic compounds) must not create a public nuisance and are assessed at DEPC permit conditions; refrigerants must be ozone-friendly and CFC-free; solid waste and food waste must be segregated and collected by the municipal waste service under the Waste Management Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Vanuatu Fire and Rescue Service covering automatic fire suppression, egress routes, extinguisher placement and kitchen exhaust cleaning; structural completion and load inspection clearances from the Port Vila Municipal Council Building Control and the Department of Public Works; occupational health and food premises clearance from the Ministry of Health Environmental Health Unit covering hand-washing facilities, ventilation, pest control and staff food-handler certificates; and workers' compensation registration where staff are engaged.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Vanuatu Department of Customs and Inland Revenue (DCIR) – official portal: https://customsinlandrevenue.gov.vu; taxpayer services via the Vanuatu Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) online registration system administered by the VAT and TIN Unit of DCIR.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign-owned International Companies (ICs) incorporated under the International Companies Act [Cap. 222] must apply for a Vanuatu TIN by submitting (1) the Application for Taxpayer Identification Number form (Form TIN-01), (2) certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation, (3) certified copy of the Registered Agent license and registered office confirmation, (4) particulars of directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners, and (5) proof of physical/virtual registered office address in Port Vila. The application may be filed by the licensed registered agent. Upon approval, DCIR issues a TIN certificate within 5–10 business days. The same TIN is used for VAT registration where applicable, though most ICs remain outside the VAT net because they conduct zero-rated or offshore activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections exist under Vanuatu law. Vanuatu imposes no corporate income tax, no capital gains tax, no withholding tax, and no estate or gift tax. An International Company is unconditionally exempt from all present and future taxes on income, assets, and transactions, subject only to the payment of annual government registration and license fees. The only relevant election is the VAT registration election under the Value Added Tax Act [Cap. 273], available to any person making taxable supplies in Vanuatu, including a non-resident IC that voluntarily registers. No hybrid mismatch election is available because Vanuatu has not enacted hybrid mismatch rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VUV 5,000,000 in taxable turnover in any 12-month period; voluntary registration permitted below threshold; mandatory registration applies to non-resident suppliers only where taxable supplies are made in Vanuatu in the course of a taxable activity carried out in Vanuatu — offshore restaurant revenue is generally outside the VAT net.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Vanuatu has not implemented real-time electronic invoicing or fiscal clearance infrastructure. There is no mandatory e-invoicing portal, no API-based continuous transaction controls (CTC), and no digital tax stamp requirement. VAT-registered businesses must issue sequential, serially numbered tax invoices in physical or PDF form containing prescribed particulars (supplier name and TIN, purchaser name and TIN for B2B supplies, date, description, quantity, price, VAT amount, and total). Records must be retained for 7 years. A phased e-invoicing reform is under study, but no statutory mandate is in force as of the applicable tax year.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under the Value Added Tax Act [Cap. 273] applies strictly to (a) the supply of goods exported from Vanuatu by the supplier, (b) the supply of services directly connected with exported goods, and (c) international transport services and services physically performed entirely outside Vanuatu. An overseas hotpot restaurant and condiment supply operation physically performed at foreign locations does not create Vanuatu VAT supply; therefore, zero-rating under Vanuatu law is not the operative relief. Instead, the overseas revenue is simply outside the scope of Vanuatu VAT because the place of supply is the foreign jurisdiction. Input VAT incurred in Vanuatu (e.g., on minor local procurement) is not attributable to taxable supplies and is generally irrecoverable unless the IC voluntarily registers for VAT and can establish that Vanuatu-sourced supplies have been made; in practice, the IC claims no refunds. Any intra-group condiment goods shipped from Vanuatu to overseas restaurants must be physically exported and supported by customs evidence to obtain zero-rating of the local supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Form CED) processed through the Vanuatu Customs Asycuda World system
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export from Vanuatu ports (Port Vila or Santo)
Inward Remittance Certificate from a licensed Vanuatu bank evidencing settlement of the export sale in foreign currency
Commercial invoice matching the export declaration
Packing list and certificate of origin (where preferential treatment claimed, though none available for hotpot condiments)
Export permit under the Vanuatu Export Control Act where food-grade condiments require phytosanitary or health certification
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DCIR and the Vanuatu Customs Service may conduct joint audits of zero-rated export claims. Penalties for fraudulent zero-rating or false export substantiation include: (1) repayment or clawback of the entire VAT refund attributable to the false claim, (2) a civil penalty of 100% of the tax sought to be evaded or a fixed penalty of up to VUV 200,000 for failure to comply with statutory record-keeping obligations, (3) interest at the statutory rate of 10% per annum on unpaid VAT, (4) criminal prosecution for tax fraud or knowingly furnishing false documentation with fines up to VUV 5,000,000 and/or imprisonment up to 7 years under the Value Added Tax Act and the Customs Act [Cap. 92], and (5) debarment of the licensed customs broker or registered agent involved in the fraudulent filing. Directors of the IC may be held personally liable where refunds are obtained without genuine physical export or where the 180-day foreign currency repatriation deadline is not met without a DCIR-approved extension.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of Vanuatu (RBV), exercising delegated exchange-control authority of the Minister of Finance under the Exchange Control Act [Cap. 138]
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Vatu (VUV) is convertible for documented current-account transactions (goods, services, invisibles) through authorized dealers, subject to prescribed exchange-control forms. Resident capital-account transfers require RBV approval, which is routinely granted for bona fide documented transactions. A Vanuatu International Company (IC) is statutorily exempt from the Exchange Control Act and is treated as a non-resident, so inward capital injections, profit repatriation, and shareholder distributions flow through unrestricted foreign-currency accounts with zero dividend withholding and zero capital-gains tax in Vanuatu. Residual practical hurdles are (i) correspondent-bank de-risking after Vanuatu's historical FATF/EU listings, (ii) heightened enhanced-due-diligence (EDD) documentation, and (iii) the shallow onshore interbank VUV market for large-liquidity conversions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For resident exporters, full export proceeds must be collected through a Vanuatu authorized dealer within 6 months from shipment date under the export declaration regime (Form E); there is no mandatory conversion ratio (0%), and proceeds may be retained in foreign currency with dealer approval. The Vanuatu IC, being exchange-control-exempt and non-resident, is subject to no surrender or conversion obligation on overseas hotpot dining receipts or condiment export proceeds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multi-currency account (USD/VUV) and foreign-currency settlement account
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account (VUV)
Operational Account and Trade Finance Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility. Leading digital EMIs (Wise, Revolut, Mercury) generally exclude Vanuatu corporate clients or impose jurisdiction-wide restrictions stemming from residual AML/CFT risk and Vanuatu's limited correspondent-banking network. Offshore EMIs that accept Pacific corporate entities require EDD packages, a substantive link to the EMI's licensed jurisdictions, and transactional caps; a Vanuatu IC holding overseas restaurant operations without domestic substance will typically fail EMI underwriting. Recommended posture: use a tier-1 Vanuatu authorized dealer as the primary clearing core and employ EMIs only as ancillary collection tools for small-ticket condiment e-commerce transactions, never for capital injection or trade settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory requirement for physical board attendance. Under the RBV AML/CFT framework and Financial Intelligence Unit guidance, Vanuatu-licensed banks may onboard a non-resident IC via a virtual video interview with directors and ultimate beneficial owners, provided the file contains certified passport copies, proof of residential address, notarized/certified certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, certificate of incumbency and UBO declaration from the registered agent, bank reference letters, and a source-of-wealth/source-of-funds statement. In practice, BRED and BSP permit virtual interviews subject to EDD; NBV may require a local managing officer or an in-person signatory visit for the initial signing mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: IC registered-agent structure with nominated non-resident shareholders or indirect ownership chains.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully populated UBO declaration identifying natural persons at or above the 25% threshold, corporate chain-of-title diagram from end-shareholder to the IC, certificate of incumbency and registered-agent attestation, passport copies and address proofs of all UBOs, source-of-wealth statement with supporting asset and tax records, and a board resolution authorizing account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive restaurant typology: high-volume cash deposits and POS settlements at overseas hotpot stores creating laundering typology concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant-acquiring and POS terminal statements for the preceding 12 months, daily sales reconciliation reports (Z-reports), supplier invoices and condiment purchase contracts, payroll and social-security filings of the operating entity, premises leases, food-safety and liquor licenses, and audited financial statements reconciling cash flows to the Vanuatu IC ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance mismatch: Vanuatu IC with no domestic activity holding funds while the active hotpot business operates in a third-country jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Offshore-holding structuring opinion from Vanuatu counsel, executed intercompany loan, licensing, and franchise agreements between the IC and the operating subsidiary, transfer-pricing documentation, operating-country business licenses and tax registrations, group organizational chart, and a projected intercompany cash-flow model with benchmarking memos.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Jurisdictional reproach: Vanuatu's prior placement on EU non-cooperative lists and FATF monitoring generating adverse media flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Certificate of Good Standing from the Vanuatu Registrar of International Companies, evidence of annual return filings, tax-information-exchange compliance confirmation, adverse-media and sanctions screening results for all UBOs, bank reference letters from prior bankers, and a compliance narrative demonstrating the entity's clean standing after regulatory remediation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder-loan funding is routed via SWIFT MT103 from the ultimate shareholder's corporate or private account to the IC's designated USD operating account at a Vanuatu authorized dealer, with remittance narrative 'INVESTMENT / SHARE CAPITAL' and the IC registration number on the beneficiary line. The supporting envelope must show a board resolution allotting shares or approving the shareholder loan, an executed loan agreement where applicable, source-of-funds evidence (bank statements, sale agreement, dividend mandate), and a UBO declaration. Since the IC is exchange-control exempt, no RBV prior approval is required for the inward credit; the bank's EDD file, however, must be complete before value dating, and the SWIFT Unique End-to-End Transaction Reference (UETR) must be archived for audit.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Routine condiment and equipment settlements use SWIFT MT103 at the authorized dealer against invoices, packing lists, and bills of lading; large recurring bulk-import programs are secured through commercial letters of credit advised via MT700/MT707, with the Vanuatu bank as issuing bank and the supplier's bank as negotiating bank, payable against compliant shipping documents. All disbursements carry explicit trade-purpose narratives (e.g., 'GOODS IMPORT' or 'ROYALTY PAYMENT'), and transactions above the dealer reporting threshold are backed by the master contract, pro-forma invoice, and transport evidence to satisfy Exchange Control Act documentation rules and correspondent-bank audit expectations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward (USD/VUV) entered with a Vanuatu authorized dealer for tenors up to 12 months, covering trade payables and receivable conversion.
Offshore non-deliverable forward (NDF) referencing VUV with a London or Singapore prime counterparty, permissible for the exchange-control-exempt non-resident IC without RBV approval.

Cross-currency swap (USD/VUV or USD/CNY) executed with a licensed non-resident bank, permitted for the IC as a non-resident exempt entity subject to bank-internal product eligibility and EDD sign-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return — statutory declaration confirming the International Company's registered office, licensed registered agent, directors, members, issued share capital and principal business activity for the reporting period (no separate filing fee; fee is subsumed in the annual fee)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) — Registrar of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing constitutes an offence under the International Companies Act [Cap 222]; the company and every defaulting officer and registered agent are liable to a fine, and a default continuing for three months or more exposes the company to a VFSC strike-off notice and administrative dissolution from the International Companies Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Fee (annual government renewal) payable for the International Company licence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the anniversary date of incorporation each year; no statutory grace period applies before late fee consequences arise
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late surcharge of 10% of the outstanding annual fee applies; if the fee remains unpaid for more than 90 days after the anniversary, the VFSC may Gazette a strike-off notice and strike the company off the International Companies Register after the statutory objection period.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation — certified update of the beneficial ownership register lodged through the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) through the VFSC-licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed concurrently with the Annual Return, within 60 calendar days after each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Submission of false, misleading or incomplete beneficial ownership particulars is an offence under the Vanuatu beneficial ownership legislation and attracts monetary penalties; persistent failure to maintain an accurate UBO register may result in the registered agent's licence being reviewed and the company being struck off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None. A Vanuatu International Company is not subject to any compulsory statutory audit, and the International Companies Act [Cap 222] prescribes no revenue, asset or shareholder threshold triggering an independent audit. A certified audit is mandatory only where the company's constitution or articles require it, shareholders so resolve, or a third-party financier (such as a bank financing the overseas hotpot restaurant operations) imposes an audit covenant.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No Vanuatu GAAP is mandatory for International Companies. Accounting records must be sufficient to explain transactions and fairly present the financial position under section 60 of the International Companies Act [Cap 222], using a recognised framework such as International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) or another acceptable foreign GAAP, and may be maintained in any currency and language at the location designated by the registered agent.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Register of Members is the controlling ownership record: every transfer of shares must be entered in the register without undue delay after the transfer instrument is approved, and the beneficial ownership position is re-derived from the updated register. At least once each year, the licensed registered agent performs a register compliance review, reconciles the share transfer instruments, director consents and minute entries, and obtains a signed annual confirmation of the identity and percentage holding of each beneficial owner from the company. The agent then lodges the prescribed Beneficial Ownership Confirmation with the VFSC together with the Annual Return. Any share transfer occurring between two confirmation dates must be reported by the company to the registered agent promptly upon registration so that the next annual confirmation accurately reflects the current shareholders.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400–1,000 per annum, being the typical annual fee charged by VFSC-licensed registered agents for provision of the registered office, corporate secretarial maintenance and filing of the annual return
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No compulsory audit is imposed on this International Company; if an audit becomes necessary by voluntary resolution or lender covenant, certified audit fees for a small-to-mid-size restaurant holding entity generally range from USD 3,000 to USD 7,500 per annum, and an unaudited accounts compilation prepared by the registered agent typically costs USD 500–1,500 per annum

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No separate tax holiday regimes. Vanuatu imposes no corporate income tax, capital gains tax, or withholding tax on any income of an International Company. Statutory fiscal obligations are limited to annual VFSC registration renewal fees and municipal business license fees.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: VFSC Annual Return and Renewal Form (IC Form AR-01) submitted via the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission online portal (eservices.vfsc.vu). No corporate income tax return exists because statutory exemption is complete.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return must be filed within 30 days after each anniversary of incorporation, and the annual renewal fee is due no later than 30 June of each calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered International Company name and registration number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact name and IC number as shown on the Certificate of Incorporation; non-resident shareholders may use English or registered transliteration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered agent name and physical address in Vanuatu.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The licensed registered agent in Vanuatu must be identified; a non-resident company cannot act as its own registered agent.
Provide the registered agent's office address or a separate physical office in Vanuatu. A post office box alone is not sufficient.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Directors, secretary, and beneficial owner particulars.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Full legal names, nationalities, residential addresses, and identification details are required for all non-resident directors and shareholders under the beneficial ownership register.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of exempt status and confirmation that no taxable activity is conducted in Vanuatu.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-controlled International Companies confirm that taxable activity is conducted wholly outside Vanuatu; local food service operations must instead be reported under a local business license.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual return attracts a penalty of VT 10,000 per month of delay, plus daily surcharges on unpaid renewal fees. Continued default results in suspension from the Register and eventual striking-off; directors and registered agents incur personal liability for outstanding government fees and penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Vanuatu has no comprehensive double taxation agreements. Because the domestic withholding rate is already nil, there is no treaty relief application to reduce statutory withholding. Where a foreign shareholder's local jurisdiction imposes CFC or deemed-dividend rules, a Vanuatu Tax Residency Certificate may be obtained through the VFSC to evidence that the International Company is not tax-resident and earned no Vanuatu-sourced taxable income. The protocol is: submit a written request to the registered agent, provide certificate of incorporation, beneficial ownership declarations, and pay VFSC certification fees.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on cross-border royalties and interest payments is 0%. No separate IP royalty code exists. Where overseas tax authorities claim taxing rights over royalty or interest paid to the offshore entity, the recipient should maintain arm's-length agreements and economic-substance evidence to support a treaty/free-zone exemption claim in the destination jurisdiction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Not applicable as Vanuatu has no transfer-pricing legislation. Best-practice threshold for foreign counterparties requesting OECD-aligned documentation: VUV 50,000,000 in connected-party annual turnover, corresponding to approximately USD 420,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vanuatu's Economic Substance Regulations are applicable to entities performing relevant activities for foreign multinational groups. Full-service hotpot dining, restaurant operations, and condiment supply to customers in Vanuatu are not designated relevant activities. However, an International Company should maintain demonstrated substance in Vanuatu through local premises, local employees, local board oversight, and locally incurred operating expenses wherever the entity receives overseas franchising, trademark, or related-party income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming International Company tax-exempt status while actively operating a restaurant, collecting domestic revenue, and deriving income from Vanuatu source without conversion to a licensed local company and payment of municipal fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Revocation of International Company registration, disgorgement of undeclared revenue equivalents, a fine of up to VUV 5,000,000, and prosecution for false declaration under the International Companies Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and registered agents are jointly and severally liable for all unpaid government fees and penalties. Travel bans may be imposed and prison terms of up to five years may apply for fraudulent use of tax-exempt status.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a nominee director and a mailbox registered agent in Vanuatu while all actual hotpot management, inventory, and daily decision-making occur in a foreign tax haven or high-tax jurisdiction, with no local employees or premises in Vanuatu and no physical presence open to customers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Striking-off from the companies register, prohibition on holding a VFSC license for ten years, and automatic referral to the FATF-style Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering for treaty-shopping risks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced: directors, even if nominee, face civil restoration of misdirected revenues, personal liability for creditor claims, travel restrictions, and disqualification as directors in any VFSC-regulated industry.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain a beneficial ownership register, accepting restaurant cash sales without suspicious transaction reporting, and permitting anonymous or shell-shareholder funds to finance the overseas hotpot chain without adequate customer due diligence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Monetary penalties up to VUV 15,000,000 for severe breaches, suspension of the foreign-exchange and merchant-acquiring licenses, compulsory reporting to the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit, and public revocation of the International Company certificate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Senior executives and directors are personally liable for AML and counter-financing of terrorism violations. Individual fines may reach VUV 2,000,000; imprisonment of up to seven years and blocking of personal bank accounts can be ordered.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Undocumented Related-Party Flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting arbitrary condiment supply prices, franchise fees, or royalty percentages between the overseas holding company and the Vanuatu International Company without contemporaneous market comparables, no invoices, and no profit allocation analysis, thereby eroding profits in high-tax jurisdictions while accumulating preferential assets in Vanuatu.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: While Vanuatu itself imposes no CIT, the VFSC may suspend the International Company for misuse of the exempt regime, and exchange-of-information requests from foreign tax authorities will be honored. Foreign jurisdictions may impose transfer-pricing adjustments, gross-up taxes, and penalties equal to 100–200% of the adjusted profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors involved in signing the pricing agreements or approving the royalty invoices may be personally assessed by foreign revenue authorities under anti-avoidance and CFC rules, and may face civil recovery actions in Vanuatu courts for breach of fiduciary duty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Commencing hotpot restaurant operations, liquor sales, or food importation in Vanuatu without the required municipal business license, food safety permit, and liquor license, or operating through the International Company as a front for an unregulated physical outlet.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Immediate closure of the restaurant premises, confiscation of equipment and condiment stock, official warnings published by municipal authorities, and cumulative fines of VUV 500,000 per day of unlicensed operation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The owning company's directors are personally liable for unpaid fines, employee unpaid wages, and supplier claims. In case of food safety negligence, criminal prosecution may result in imprisonment of up to three years and a lifetime ban from obtaining a Vanuatu business license.
